symptom: A delivery candidate could be considered merge-ready after the normal workflow checks were green while separate GitHub App checks on the same head commit were still pending or non-successful.
GitHub Advanced Security can publish an independent CodeQL check-run that is not represented by the normal Powerhouse workflow result.
root_cause: Terminal delivery authority previously reasoned from a required-check subset instead of the full check-run and legacy-status set attached to the exact candidate head SHA.
Security-provided neutral results were not distinguished from informational neutral results.
prevention: Bind terminal delivery to the exact candidate head SHA.
Read the complete commit check-run set and legacy commit statuses before merge.
Block on queued, in_progress, pending, failure, cancelled, timed_out, action_required or stale evidence.
Treat neutral/skipped security checks as blocking unless explicitly proven terminal-safe by policy; informational non-security neutral checks may remain evidence.
Keep required checks as a mandatory subset, never as the complete delivery truth.
Re-read exact head, current main epoch, full checkset and mergeability immediately before terminal merge.
After merge, require production/readback terminalization before the obligation can become green.
failed_approaches: Using the normal Required test / workflow outcome as a proxy for all checks attached to a commit.
Declaring merge readiness before GitHub Advanced Security and provider checks had reached a terminal policy-accepted state.
